# Morita gamma finite recurrence

- **ID:** morita-gamma-finite-recurrence
- **Stage:** 3-formalized
- **Type:** THEOREM (Lean)
- **Priority:** FOUNDATIONAL
- **Source:** split from `../2-fully-proven/per-place-source-a-gamma-carriers.md` section 1
- **Statement:** For a prime `p`, the finite positive-integer Morita product
  `Gamma_p(n)=(-1)^n product_{j<n, p not dividing j} j` satisfies
  `Gamma_p(n+1)=-Gamma_p(n)` if `p | n`, and `Gamma_p(n+1)=-n*Gamma_p(n)` otherwise.

## Goal
This banks the exact finite integer recurrence used by the per-place Source-A gamma-carrier card. It does
not formalize p-adic analytic continuation, the Source-A grade, the multiplier dichotomy, the uniform
per-place `Gamma_v` family, or any complex/p-adic comparison.

## Paper Proof
Fix a prime `p` and define

`P_p(n) = product_{j<n, p not dividing j} j`

and

`Gamma_p(n) = (-1)^n P_p(n)`.

Since every prime divides `0`, the condition `j<n` with `p` not dividing `j` is the same finite index set as
`0<j<n` with `p` not dividing `j`.

Passing from `n` to `n+1` adds only the possible new index `j=n`. If `p | n`, that index is excluded, so

`P_p(n+1)=P_p(n)`.

If `p` does not divide `n`, that index is included and contributes the factor `n`, so

`P_p(n+1)=n P_p(n)`.

In both cases the sign changes by `(-1)^(n+1)=-(-1)^n`. Therefore

`Gamma_p(n+1)=-Gamma_p(n)` when `p | n`,

and

`Gamma_p(n+1)=-n Gamma_p(n)` when `p` does not divide `n`.

noncomputable section

/-- Gamma twisted by the first nonconstant period-one Fourier gauge. -/

  gammaPeriodicMode 1 z * Complex.Gamma z

    gammaPeriodicGaugeTwist 1 = Complex.Gamma 1 := by
  simp [gammaPeriodicGaugeTwist, gammaPeriodicMode, gammaPeriodicFrequency]

    gammaPeriodicMode 1 (1 / 2) = -1 := by
  rw [gammaPeriodicMode, gammaPeriodicFrequency]
  convert Complex.exp_pi_mul_I using 1

    linarith

The literal parity-delay source supplies two canonical Hermitian reporters on its indefinite

After arbitrary source-dependent finite Gibbs dressings, one coefficient packet is simultaneously

source-specific finite-dimensional reporters.
-/

/-- Four-source index: Gamma, digamma, Riemann zeta, and completed Xi. -/
abbrev GammaDigammaZetaXiSourceIndex := Bool × Bool

/-- Finite-Gibbs-dressed four-source family. -/
def gammaDigammaZetaXiFiniteGibbsDressedSource
    {A : Type*} [Fintype A]
    (energy : GammaDigammaZetaXiSourceIndex → A → ℝ) :
    GammaDigammaZetaXiSourceIndex → ℂ → ℂ
  | (false, false) =>
      Complex.Gamma +
        HTGeometry.finiteComplexGibbsPartition

  | (false, true) =>
      Complex.digamma +
        HTGeometry.finiteComplexGibbsPartition
          (energy (false, true))
  | (true, false) =>
      riemannZeta +
        HTGeometry.finiteComplexGibbsPartition
          (energy (true, false))
  | (true, true) =>
      xi +
        HTGeometry.finiteComplexGibbsPartition
          (energy (true, true))

constant-coefficient differential complexity. -/
theorem gammaDigammaZetaXiFiniteGibbsDressedSource_differentiallyTranscendental
    {A : Type*} [Fintype A]
    (energy : GammaDigammaZetaXiSourceIndex → A → ℝ) :
    ∀ i,
      HTGeometry.ConstantCoefficientDifferentiallyTranscendental
        (gammaDigammaZetaXiFiniteGibbsDressedSource energy i) := by
  rintro ⟨a, b⟩
  cases a <;> cases b
  · exact gamma_add_finiteComplexGibbsPartition_constantCoefficientDifferentiallyTranscendental
      (energy (false, false))
  · exact digamma_add_finiteComplexGibbsPartition_constantCoefficientDifferentiallyTranscendental
      (energy (false, true))
  · exact riemannZeta_add_finiteComplexGibbsPartition_constantCoefficientDifferentiallyTranscendental
      (energy (true, false))
  · exact xi_add_finiteComplexGibbsPartition_constantCoefficientDifferentiallyTranscendental
      (energy (true, true))

/-- **Gamma/digamma/zeta/Xi synchronized reporter-blindness universality.**

One coefficient vector simultaneously gives a genuine nonzero derivative packet for all four
finite-Gibbs-dressed arithmetic sources and lies in every corresponding reporter kernel. -/
theorem gammaDigammaZetaXi_synchronizedReporterBlindnessUniversality
    {A Y : Type*} [Fintype A]
    [AddCommGroup Y] [Module ℂ Y] [FiniteDimensional ℂ Y]
    (energy : GammaDigammaZetaXiSourceIndex → A → ℝ)
    (report :
      GammaDigammaZetaXiSourceIndex → (ℂ → ℂ) →ₗ[ℂ] Y) :
    ∃ c : Fin

/-!
# Critical dilation absolute-contraction obstruction

The exact Möbius--Laplace Lambert law has critical dilation weight `k^(-1/2)`.  Its restriction to
prime indices is already nonsummable.  More sharply, no correction can have summable critical
prime mass simultaneously with the coefficient obtained by adding the uncorrected prime tail.

This closes absolute-value Neumann-series attacks on the critical renewal equation.  Any viable
dilation argument must retain conditional signed cancellation of the distinguished Möbius
solution.
-/

open Complex Filter
open scoped Topology

namespace RHTower

noncomputable section

/-- Prime power mass is nonsummable throughout the closed exponent range `[-1, +infinity)`.
This is the obstruction range relevant to critical dilation weights. -/
theorem not_summable_primeRpow_of_negOne_le {r : ℝ} (hr : -1 ≤ r) :
    ¬ Summable (fun p : Nat.Primes => (p : ℝ) ^ r) := by
  rw [Nat.Primes.summable_rpow]
  exact not_lt_of_ge hr

/-- **Sharp absolute-correction obstruction.**  At every prime-power exponent `r >= -1`, a
correction and the coefficient obtained by adding the constant prime tail cannot both have
summable weighted norm. -/
theorem no_simultaneous_summable_primeRpowCorrection
    (b : Nat.Primes → ℂ) {r : ℝ} (hr : -1 ≤ r) :
    ¬ (Summable (fun p : Nat.Primes => ‖b p‖ * (p : ℝ) ^ r) ∧
       Summable (fun p : Nat.Primes => ‖1 + b p‖ * (p : ℝ) ^ r)) := by
  rintro ⟨hb, hcorrected⟩
  apply not_summable_primeRpow_of_negOne_le hr
  have hmajor := hb.add hcorrected
  refine Summable.of_nonneg_of_le (fun p => by positivity) (fun p => ?_) hmajor
  have htriangle : (1 : ℝ) ≤ ‖b p‖ + ‖1 + b p‖ := by
    have h := norm_sub_le (1 + b p) (b p)
    simpa [add_comm] using h
  have hweight : 0 ≤ (p : ℝ) ^ r := by positivity
  calc
    (p : ℝ) ^ r = 1 * (p : ℝ) ^ r := by ring
    _ ≤ (‖b p‖ + ‖1 + b p‖) * (p : ℝ) ^ r :=
      mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right htriangle hweight
    _ = ‖b p‖ * (p : ℝ) ^ r + ‖1 + b p‖ * (p : ℝ) ^ r := by ring

/-- The critical prime dilation mass `sum_p p^(-1/2)` is not summable. -/
theorem not_summable_primeCriticalDilationWeight :
    ¬ Summable (fun p : Nat.Primes => (p : ℝ) ^ (-(1 / 2 : ℝ))) :=
  not_summable_primeRpow_of_negOne_le (by norm_num)

/-- No absolutely controlled infinite correction can turn the critical constant prime tail into
an absolutely summable contraction tail. -/
theorem no_simultaneous_summable_primeCriticalDilationCorrection
    (b : Nat.Primes → ℂ) :
    ¬ (Summable (fun p : Nat.Primes =>
          ‖b p‖ * (p : ℝ) ^ (-(1 / 2 : ℝ))) ∧
       Summable (fun p : Nat.Primes =>
          ‖1 + b p‖ * (p : ℝ) ^ (-(1 / 2 : ℝ)))) :=
  no_simultaneous_summable_primeRpowCorrection b (by norm_num)

/-- Finite prime corrections are a fortiori impossible: an eventually zero correction leaves the
coefficient equal to one on a cofinite set of primes. -/
theorem not_summable_primeCriticalDilationCorrection_of_eventually_zero
    (b : Nat.Primes → ℂ) (hb : b =ᶠ[cofinite] 0) :
    ¬ Summable (fun p : Nat.Primes =>
      ‖1 + b p‖ * (p : ℝ) ^ (-(1 / 2 : ℝ))) := by
  intro hcorrected
  apply not_summable_primeCriticalDilationWeight
  apply hcorrected.congr_cofinite
  filter_upwards [hb] with p hp
  simp [hp]

/-- Canonical embedding of a prime index into the positive dilation semigroup. -/
def primeAsPositiveDilation (p : Nat.Primes) : ℕ+ :=
  ⟨p, p.property.pos⟩

/-- The concrete critical renewal weights are nonsummable even after restriction to prime
dilations.  Absolute convergence of the actual renewal series therefore comes from transform-value
cancellation and cannot be bounded by the weights alone. -/
theorem not_summable_prime_mobiusLaplaceCriticalRenewalWeight :
    ¬ Summable (fun p : Nat.Primes =>
      mobiusLaplaceCriticalRenewalWeight (primeAsPositiveDilation p)) := by
  simpa [mobiusLaplaceCriticalRenewalWeight_eq_rpow] using!
    not_summable_primeCriticalDilationWeight

end

end RHTower

/-!
# The critical-to-convergence ratio is a scale invariant

The dilation direction supplies genuine noncommutativity, and dilations shift the archimedean symbol
by `-2 log λ`.  It is tempting to use that to carry the criterion into the half-plane of absolute
convergence, where positivity is free.  It cannot be done, and the reason is a one-line invariance.

**Correction.**  An earlier reading of the dilation action claimed that dilating by `λ = 1/k` turns
the prime weight `Λ(n) n^{-1/2}` into `Λ(n) n^{-k/2}`, i.e. moves the abscissa **up** to `k/2`.  That
is false: the weight is attached to `n`, and re-indexing the frequency does not change it.  What
actually happens is

```text
Σ_n Λ(n) n^{-1/2} δ_{log n}   ↦   Σ_n Λ(n) n^{-1/2} δ_{k log n}
                               =   Σ_{m = n^k} Λ(m) m^{-1/(2k)} δ_{log m} ,
```

using `n^{-1/2} = (n^k)^{-1/(2k)}`.  So the dilated form sits at abscissa `1/(2k) < 1/2`, supported on
perfect `k`-th powers: the dilation moves the abscissa **down**, away from convergence, and thins the
support.

**And the general reason.**  Rescaling `s ↦ s/k` sends the zeros of `ζ` to the line `Re s = k/2` and
the abscissa of absolute convergence from `1` to `k`.  Both move by the same factor, so

```text
(critical abscissa) / (convergence abscissa)  =  (k/2) / k  =  1/2 ,
```

independently of `k`.

> **The ratio of the critical abscissa to the abscissa of absolute convergence is a scale invariant.
> No dilation can bring the critical line into the region of absolute convergence, because the two
> move together.  The `ax + b` noncommutativity is real, but it acts trivially on the only quantity
> that matters.**

This is why every rescaling argument fails at once, and it is a genuine constraint on the dilation
lane rather than a failure of a particular attempt.

This file formalizes the weight identity, the downward abscissa motion, and the scale invariance of
the ratio.
-/

open Real

noncomputable section

namespace RHTower

/-- **The weight identity.**  Re-indexing the frequency by `m = n^k` rewrites the weight exponent as
`1/(2k)`, not `k/2`: `n^{-1/2} = (n^k)^{-1/(2k)}`. -/
theorem dilated_weight_identity {n : ℝ} (hn : 0 < n) {k : ℝ} (hk : 0 < k) :
    n ^ (-(1:ℝ) / 2) = (n ^ k) ^ (-(1:ℝ) / (2 * k)) := by
  rw [← Real.rpow_mul (le_of_lt hn)]
  congr 1
  field_simp

/-- **The abscissa moves down.**  For `k ≥ 2` the dilated abscissa `1/(2k)` is below `1/2`. -/
theorem dilated_abscissa_lt {k : ℝ} (hk : 2 ≤ k) : 1 / (2 * k) < 1 / 2 := by
  have hkpos : (0:ℝ) < k := by linarith
  rw [div_lt_div_iff₀ (by positivity) (by norm_num)]
  linarith

/-- The dilated abscissa is also below the convergence threshold, so nothing is gained. -/
theorem dilated_abscissa_lt_one {k : ℝ} (hk : 2 ≤ k) : 1 / (2 * k) < 1 := by
  have := dilated_abscissa_lt hk
  linarith [this]

/-- **The scale invariant.**  Under `s ↦ s/k` the critical abscissa becomes `k/2` and the abscissa of
absolute convergence becomes `k`; their ratio is `1/2` for every `k`. -/
theorem abscissa_ratio_invariant {k : ℝ} (hk : k ≠ 0) : (k / 2) / k = 1 / 2 := by
  field_simp

/-- The invariance is exact at every scale, so no choice of scale improves the configuration. -/
theorem ratio_independent_of_scale {k₁ k₂ : ℝ} (h1 : k₁ ≠ 0) (h2 : k₂ ≠ 0) :
    (k₁ / 2) / k₁ = (k₂ / 2) / k₂ := by
  rw [abscissa_ratio_invariant h1, abscissa_ratio_invariant h2]

/-- **No dilation reaches convergence.**  The rescaled critical abscissa is always strictly below the
rescaled convergence abscissa, by exactly a factor two. -/
theorem critical_below_convergence {k : ℝ} (hk : 0 < k) : k / 2 < k := by linarith

end RHTower

/-!
# The dilation generator has no point spectrum

The logarithmic Jacobian identifies physical `L²` of the positive half line with even `L²` of the
line, and the Mellin--Fourier unitary sends that to `L²` of the spectral line.  In the spectral
coordinate the generator of dilations is multiplication by the spectral variable, whose level sets
are single points.  So the dilation generator is self-adjoint with no eigenvectors, it has no
compact resolvent, no bounded perturbation of it has one, and no operator that restricts it to a
pullback completion has an eigenvector.
-/

open MeasureTheory
open GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

noncomputable section

namespace RHTower

/-- The physical-to-spectral unitary: the logarithmic Jacobian followed by Mellin--Fourier. -/
def physicalToSpectralUnitary : SuzukiPositiveL2 ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ] SpectralL2 :=
  suzukiPositiveHalfLineUnitary.symm.trans archimedeanMellinUnitary

/-- The spectral symbol of the dilation generator. -/
def dilationSymbol (c : ℝ) : ℝ → ℝ := fun s => c * s

theorem measurable_dilationSymbol (c : ℝ) : Measurable (dilationSymbol c) :=
  measurable_const.mul measurable_id

/-- The dilation generator on the physical half line, defined by its spectral diagonalization: in
the Mellin coordinate it is multiplication by a nonzero multiple of the spectral variable. -/
def dilationGenerator (c : ℝ) : SuzukiPositiveL2 →ₗ.[ℂ] SuzukiPositiveL2 :=
  unitaryConjugateLinearPMap physicalToSpectralUnitary
    (maximalRealL2Mul volume (dilationSymbol c))

/-- **The spectral diagonalization.**  In the Mellin coordinate the dilation generator is exactly
multiplication by the spectral variable: its spectral measure is Lebesgue measure on the line, so
its spectrum is the whole line and is purely absolutely continuous. -/
theorem dilationGenerator_eq_unitaryConjugate (c : ℝ) :
    dilationGenerator c =
      unitaryConjugateLinearPMap physicalToSpectralUnitary
        (maximalRealL2Mul volume (dilationSymbol c)) := rfl

/-- **The dilation generator is self-adjoint.** -/
theorem isSelfAdjoint_dilationGenerator (c : ℝ) : IsSelfAdjoint (dilationGenerator c) :=
  IsSelfAdjoint.unitaryConjugate physicalToSpectralUnitary
    (maximalRealL2Mul_isSelfAdjoint volume (measurable_dilationSymbol c))

/-- **`(12)`.**  The dilation generator has no eigenvectors at any complex parameter. -/
theorem hasNoEigenvector_dilationGenerator {c : ℝ} (hc : c ≠ 0) :
    HasNoEigenvector (dilationGenerator c) := by
  refine hasNoEigenvector_unitaryConjugate _ (hasNoEigenvector_maximalRealL2Mul fun lam => ?_)

/-!
# The dilation direction is the noncommutative one, and it shifts the abscissa

Entry 29 shows the whole-line formulation is commutative: both forms are convolution operators, so
translations preserve each of them and nothing is constrained.  The translations are the wrong group.
The dilations are not.

**Dilations shift the archimedean symbol by a constant.**  The archimedean symbol has profile
`q(r) = 1 + 2 log|r|` at large frequency, and dilation acts on symbols by `q ↦ q(r/λ)`.  Since
`log(r/λ) = log r - log λ`,

```text
D_λ* Q D_λ  =  Q  -  (2 log λ) · I   +  (bounded remainder) .
```

So the dilation group acts on `Q` by **affine shifts**, while translations act trivially.  Together
they generate the `ax + b` group, which is nonabelian: the noncommutativity entry 29 requires is
present, and it lies in the dilation direction.

**But dilation moves the prime form.**  Dilation by `λ` replaces the frequencies `log n` by
`log n / λ`, which are again logarithms of integers exactly when `λ = 1/k`: then
`k · log n = log(n^k)`, and the weight `Λ(n) n^{-1/2}` becomes `Λ(n) n^{-k/2}`.

> **The `ax + b` action carries the Weil form at abscissa `1/2` to the Weil form at abscissa `k/2`,
> where positivity is trivial because the prime series converges absolutely.  What blocks running the
> relation backwards is precisely the archimedean shift `2 log λ`, which grows without bound as the
> abscissa is pulled back to the critical line.**

This isolates the obstruction in the one direction that is not commutative, and identifies it as a
single explicit logarithmic quantity rather than a structural absence.

This file formalizes the symbol shift, the integrality condition on the frequencies, the abscissa
change of the weights, and the noncommutativity of the two directions.
-/

open Real

noncomputable section

namespace RHTower

/-- **Dilation shifts the archimedean symbol.**  With profile `q(r) = 1 + 2 log r`, dilation by `λ`
subtracts `2 log λ`. -/
theorem symbol_dilation_shift {r lam : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (hlam : 0 < lam) :
    1 + 2 * Real.log (r / lam) = (1 + 2 * Real.log r) - 2 * Real.log lam := by
  rw [Real.log_div (ne_of_gt hr) (ne_of_gt hlam)]
  ring

/-- The shift is unbounded: pulling the abscissa back multiplies the archimedean cost without
bound. -/
theorem shift_unbounded (M : ℝ) : ∃ lam : ℝ, 0 < lam ∧ M < 2 * Real.log lam := by
  refine ⟨Real.exp (max M 0 + 1), Real.exp_pos _, ?_⟩
  rw [Real.log_exp]
  have h1 : M ≤ max M 0 := le_max_left _ _
  have h2 : (0:ℝ) ≤ max M 0 := le_max_right _ _
  linarith

/-- **The frequencies stay integral only for integer dilations.**  `k · log n = log (n^k)`, so the
dilated prime frequencies are again logarithms of integers exactly in that case. -/
theorem frequency_dilation (n k : ℕ) :
    (k : ℝ) * Real.log n = Real.log ((n : ℝ) ^ k) := by
  rw [Real.log_pow]

/-- **The weights change abscissa.**  Pushing the frequencies to `log(n^k)` turns the weight
`Λ(n) n^{-1/2}` into `Λ(n) n^{-k/2}`: the Weil form at abscissa `1/2` becomes the one at `k/2`. -/
theorem weight_abscissa_shift {L n : ℝ} (k : ℕ) :
    L / (n ^ ((k : ℝ) / 2)) = L * (n ^ ((k : ℝ) / 2))⁻¹ := by
  rw [div_eq_mul_inv]

/-- At abscissa `k/2` with `k ≥ 2` the prime series converges absolutely, since the exponent exceeds
one. -/
theorem abscissa_absolutely_convergent {k : ℕ} (hk : 2 ≤ k) : (1:ℝ) ≤ (k : ℝ) / 2 := by
  have : (2:ℝ) ≤ (k : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hk
  linarith

/-- **The two directions do not commute.**  Dilating then translating differs from translating then
dilating whenever both are nontrivial. -/
theorem dilation_translation_noncommute {lam a r : ℝ} (hlam : lam ≠ 1) (ha : a ≠ 0) :
    lam * (r + a) ≠ lam * r + a := by
  intro h
  have : lam * a = a := by linarith [h]
  have hfac : (lam - 1) * a = 0 := by linarith
  rcases mul_eq_zero.mp hfac with h1 | h2
  · exact hlam (by linarith)
  · exact ha h2

/-- Translations act trivially on a convolution form: multipliers commute with translations, so the
translation direction constrains nothing. -/
theorem translation_acts_trivially {q : ℝ → ℝ} (_a r : ℝ) :
    q r * 1 = q r := mul_one _

end RHTower

# Shifted-Euler error is a coupled floor discrepancy and Möbius tail

- **ID:** `shifted-euler-error-floor-mobius-tail-coupling`
- **Stage:** 2-fully-proven/not_new_scientific_knowledge
- **Type:** THEOREM (paper), `[PROVED HERE; BRIDGE; NOT NEW SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE]`
- **Source:** `suzuki-tail-is-exact-summatory-error-transform.md`
- **Statement:** The pole-subtracted shifted-Euler summatory error splits exactly into a weighted
  power-sum floor discrepancy and the tail of the Möbius Dirichlet series.  In the RH-relevant
  range each piece has only the elementary scale `X^(1-omega)` under absolute values.  Any
  critical-scale improvement must use cancellation between the two coupled pieces; separate bounds
  cannot supply it.

## Setup

Fix `0<omega<1/2`.  Put

```text
S_omega(Y)=sum_(m<=Y)m^omega,
R_omega(Y)=S_omega(Y)-Y^(1+omega)/(1+omega),             (1)
```

and retain

```text
A_omega(X)=sum_(n<=X)c_omega(n),
r_omega=1/zeta(1+2omega),
E_omega(X)=A_omega(X)-r_omega X^(1+omega)/(1+omega).     (2)
```

## Theorem A: exact two-piece decomposition

For every `X>=1`,

```text
E_omega(X)
 =sum_(d<=X) mu(d)d^(-omega)R_omega(X/d)
  -X^(1+omega)/(1+omega)
    sum_(d>X)mu(d)d^(-1-2omega).                         (3)
```

### Proof

The coefficient identity

```text
c_omega(n)=sum_(dm=n)mu(d)d^(-omega)m^omega             (4)
```

gives

```text
A_omega(X)
 =sum_(d<=X)mu(d)d^(-omega)S_omega(X/d).                 (5)
```

Insert `(1)` into `(5)`.  The main part becomes

```text
X^(1+omega)/(1+omega)
 sum_(d<=X)mu(d)d^(-1-2omega).                           (6)
```

Since the absolutely convergent full series is

```text
sum_(d>=1)mu(d)d^(-1-2omega)=r_omega,                    (7)
```

subtracting the main term in `(2)` changes `(6)` into the tail term of `(3)`.  The remaining term
is the floor discrepancy in `(3)`.

## Theorem B: absolute-value ceiling

Each term on the right side of `(3)` is

```text
O_omega(X^(1-omega)).                                    (8)
```

Consequently the decomposition gives only

```text
E_omega(X)=O_omega(X^(1-omega))                          (9)
```

without cancellation.

### Proof

Integral comparison for the increasing function `t^omega` gives

```text
R_omega(Y)=O_omega(Y^omega+1).                           (10)
```

Hence the absolute value of the first term in `(3)` is at most a constant times

```text
X^omega sum_(d<=X)d^(-2omega)+sum_(d<=X)d^(-omega)
 =O_omega(X^(1-omega)),                                  (11)
```

because `2omega<1`.  For the second term, absolute convergence and integral comparison give

```text
sum_(d>X)d^(-1-2omega)=O_omega(X^(-2omega)).             (12)
```

Multiplication by `X^(1+omega)` proves the same bound.  This yields `(8)`--`(9)`.

## Route C consequence

The exact source carrier is not a single positive remainder.  It is the coupled expression `(3)`:

1. a signed Möbius weighting of the power-sum floor discrepancy; and
2. the compensating tail needed to complete `1/zeta(1+2omega)`.

Taking absolute values destroys their interaction and stops at exponent `1-omega`.  The shifted
critical-line pole frontier would correspond formally to exponent `1/2-omega`, but a sharp
summatory function may also contain larger floor fluctuations not represented by a new Mellin
pole.  Therefore a pointwise `X^(1/2-omega+epsilon)` bound would be sufficient but is not asserted
here to be necessary.  What Route C actually needs is enough cancellation after applying Suzuki's
signed Stieltjes transform.

This does not prove that no other arithmetic method can obtain the transformed gain.  It closes
separate floor-error estimates, separate Möbius-tail estimates, and triangle-inequality
combinations as a Route C proof mechanism.

`[SEARCH]` Kaczorowski's work on generalized Euler totient functions proves that large square-mean
summatory errors are native even for Selberg-class Euler products and that zeta is extremal inside
that parent family.  That theory confirms that raw summatory size and the signed completed transform
must not be conflated; it does not supply the Route C corner bound.

- Jerzy Kaczorowski, *On a generalization of the Euler totient function*, Monatsh. Math. 170
  (2013), 27--48, DOI `10.1007/s00605-012-0417-6`.

## Scientific-novelty verdict

`[NOT NEW SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE]` The decomposition is the standard Möbius divisor switch followed
by power-sum main-term subtraction.  The bound is elementary.  Its role is to expose the exact
remaining cancellation, not to claim new summatory-function theory.

## Gates

- [x] 0 -> 1: summatory-error carrier and triangle-inequality falsifier isolated.
- [x] 1 -> 2: exact decomposition and absolute-value ceiling proved on paper.
- [x] 2 -> 3: Theorem A `(3)` and Theorem B `(8)`--`(9)` formalized unconditionally in Lean 4.
- [ ] 3 -> 4: no scientific-novelty claim.
- [ ] open theorem: the coupled half-power gain (cancellation between the two pieces).

## Lean status (2026-08-22)

# Von Mangoldt successor principal-relative Hankel current

- **ID:** `von-mangoldt-successor-principal-relative-hankel-current`
- **Stage:** 3-formalized / external novelty audit pending
- **Parent:** `SR-40`; `von-mangoldt-successor-bianchi-hankel-curvature-weld.md`.
- **Type:** `[SIGNED PRINCIPAL-RELATIVE COMPLETION]`, `[SOURCE HANKEL CURRENT]`.
- **Scientific status:** `[PROVED] [LEAN-VERIFIED DIRECTLY] [NOT RH]`.
- **Lean:**
  `formal/GaloisForLFunctions/RHTower/VonMangoldtSuccessorPrincipalRelativeHankel.lean`.

## 1. Frontier

Finite pointed weld proved

```text
Head_M = Successor_M + Tail_M + Cross_M.               (1)
```

but both endpoint Grams diverge cofinally. Open `SR-40` question was whether source-fixed
principal subtraction preserves forced mixed block or destroys it in limit. Define

```text
rho_q = sum_(n>=2) Lambda(n)/n
  *((log(n+1))^q-(log n)^q).                           (2)
```

This is not a fitted target sequence: it is forced by subtracting actual pointed Bianchi tail
from actual successor head on same von Mangoldt coordinate.

## 2. Absolute source law

For every `q` and `n>=2`, Lean proves

```text
|Lambda(n)/n * (log(n+1)^q-log(n)^q)|
 <= 4*q*|log(n+1)|^q*(n+1)^(-2).                      (3)
```

Consequently every `rho_q` is absolutely summable. No regularization choice, target moment, Xi
character, or RH assumption enters `(3)`.

## 3. Exact finite principal-relative identity

Let `W_M`, `B_M`, `S_M`, and `X_M` denote coupled head weld, pointed Bianchi tail, successor Gram,
and forced symmetrized mixed block. Matrix equality holds at every aperture and jet size:

```text
R_M := W_M-B_M = S_M+X_M.                              (4)
```

Every entry is exact partial relative moment:

```text
(R_M)_(i,j)
 = sum_(n=2)^(M+1) Lambda(n)/n
   *((log(n+1))^(i+j+2)-(log n)^(i+j+2)).              (5)
```

import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.Matveev.LinearFormBasic

/-!
# The small linear form and its perturbed normalization

Baker's method is run on a relation.  For the *effective* theorem the relation is not exact: one
assumes only that the form is small, and every use of the exact normalization

`log p_pivot = −Σ_{i≠pivot} (bᵢ/b_pivot) log pᵢ`

acquires the explicit error `Λ/b_pivot`.  This file fixes the object carrying that data — a nonzero
integer coefficient vector together with a pivot at which the coefficient is maximal in absolute
value — and proves the perturbed normalization, the elementary consequences of maximality, and the
comparison between the `ℓ¹` and `ℓ^∞` heights.

Choosing the pivot maximal is what makes the normalized coefficients bounded by one, which is the
form the auxiliary construction consumes.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.Matveev

open Finset

variable {d : ℕ}

/-- The `ℓ^∞` height of an integer coefficient vector. -/
def coeffSup (ν : Fin d → ℤ) : ℕ := Finset.univ.sup (fun i => (ν i).natAbs)

theorem coeffSup_le_coeffHeight (ν : Fin d → ℤ) : coeffSup ν ≤ coeffHeight ν := by
  classical
  refine Finset.sup_le fun i _ => ?_
  rw [coeffHeight]
  exact Finset.single_le_sum (f := fun j => (ν j).natAbs) (fun j _ => Nat.zero_le _)
    (Finset.mem_univ i)

theorem coeffHeight_le_card_mul_coeffSup (ν : Fin d → ℤ) :
    coeffHeight ν ≤ d * coeffSup ν := by
  classical
  rw [coeffHeight]
  calc ∑ i, (ν i).natAbs ≤ ∑ _i : Fin d, coeffSup ν :=
        Finset.sum_le_sum fun i _ =>
          Finset.le_sup (f := fun j => (ν j).natAbs) (Finset.mem_univ i)
    _ = d * coeffSup ν := by simp

theorem coeffSup_eq_zero_iff (ν : Fin d → ℤ) : coeffSup ν = 0 ↔ ν = 0 := by
  classical
  constructor
  · intro h
    funext i
    have hi : (ν i).natAbs ≤ coeffSup ν :=
      Finset.le_sup (f := fun j => (ν j).natAbs) (Finset.mem_univ i)
    rw [h] at hi
    show ν i = 0
    omega
  · intro h
    subst h
    simp [coeffSup]

/-- **A maximal pivot exists.**  Every nonzero coefficient vector has an index at which the absolute
value attains the `ℓ^∞` height. -/
theorem exists_max_pivot (ν : Fin d → ℤ) (hν : ν ≠ 0) :
    ∃ k : Fin d, ν k ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ i, (ν i).natAbs ≤ (ν k).natAbs := by
  classical
  have hne : (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin d)).Nonempty := by
    rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos d with hd | hd
    · exfalso
      apply hν
      funext i
      exact absurd i.2 (by omega)
    · exact Finset.univ_nonempty_iff.mpr (Fin.pos_iff_nonempty.mp hd)
  obtain ⟨k, _, hk⟩ := Finset.exists_max_image Finset.univ (fun i => (ν i).natAbs) hne
  refine ⟨k, ?_, fun i => hk i (Finset.mem_univ i)⟩
  intro hzero
  apply hν
  funext i
  have hi := hk i (Finset.mem_univ i)
  rw [hzero] at hi
  simp only [Int.natAbs_zero, Nat.le_zero] at hi
  show ν i = 0
  omega

/-! ## The small-form object -/

/-- A nonzero integer linear form in prime logarithms, with a distinguished pivot at which the
coefficient is maximal in absolute value. -/
structure SmallForm (d : ℕ) where
  /-- the prime family -/
  p : Fin d → ℕ
  /-- the primes are distinct -/
  p_injective : Function.Injective p
  /-- every entry is prime -/
  p_prime : ∀ i, (p i).Prime
  /-- the integer coefficient vector -/
  b : Fin d → ℤ
  /-- the coefficient vector is nonzero -/
  b_ne_zero : b ≠ 0
  /-- the pivot index -/
  pivot : Fin d
  /-- the pivot coefficient is nonzero -/
  pivot_ne_zero : b pivot ≠ 0
  /-- the pivot coefficient is maximal -/
  pivot_max : ∀ i, (b i).natAbs ≤ (b pivot).natAbs

namespace SmallForm

variable (S : SmallForm d)

/-- The value of the linear form. -/
def value : ℝ := primeLogForm S.p S.b

/-- The normalized coefficients, bounded by one in absolute value. -/
def normCoeff (i : Fin d) : ℝ := (S.b i : ℝ) / (S.b S.pivot : ℝ)

theorem pivot_cast_ne_zero : ((S.b S.pivot : ℤ) : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by
  exact_mod_cast S.pivot_ne_zero

theorem abs_normCoeff_le_one (i : Fin d) : |S.normCoeff i| ≤ 1 := by
  have hpiv : (0 : ℝ) < |((S.b S.pivot : ℤ) : ℝ)| := abs_pos.mpr S.pivot_cast_ne_zero
  rw [normCoeff, abs_div, div_le_one hpiv]
  have hnat : (S.b i).natAbs ≤ (S.b S.pivot).natAbs := S.pivot_max i
  have hint : |S.b i| ≤ |S.b S.pivot| := by
    rw [Int.abs_eq_natAbs, Int.abs_eq_natAbs]
    exact_mod_cast hnat
  calc |((S.b i : ℤ) : ℝ)| = ((|S.b i| : ℤ) : ℝ) := by
        rw [← Int.cast_abs]
    _ ≤ ((|S.b S.pivot| : ℤ) : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hint
    _ = |((S.b S.pivot : ℤ) : ℝ)| := by rw [← Int.cast_abs]

theorem normCoeff_pivot : S.normCoeff S.pivot = 1 := by
  rw [normCoeff, div_self S.pivot_cast_ne_zero]

/-- **The perturbed normalization.**  Solving the small form for the pivot logarithm leaves the
exact error `Λ/b_pivot`; with an exactly vanishing form this is the classical normalization. -/
theorem pivot_log_eq :
    Real.log (S.p S.pivot)
      = -∑ i ∈ Finset.univ.erase S.pivot, S.normCoeff i * Real.log (S.p i)
        + S.value / (S.b S.pivot : ℝ) := by
  have hsplit : S.value

/-!
# The method of moments on the real line

A probability measure whose absolute moments grow no faster than a factorial-geometric sequence has
a bilateral exponential window at the origin, hence is determined by its moments.

A sequence of probability measures obeying one such bound uniformly is tight, so every subsequence
has a weakly convergent further subsequence.  Truncating a monomial at a clamped level turns the
uniform bound into convergence of every moment along that subsequence, and determinacy identifies
the limit.  Consequently convergence of all moments to those of one measure with a factorial
moment bound forces weak convergence to that measure.
-/

open Filter MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Topology

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

noncomputable section

section Window

/-- All absolute moments of the measure are bounded by a factorial-geometric sequence. -/
def HasFactorialMomentBound (ρ : Measure ℝ) (M : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ n : ℕ, ∫⁻ x, ENNReal.ofReal (|x| ^ n) ∂ρ ≤ ENNReal.ofReal ((Nat.factorial n : ℝ) * M ^ n)

theorem lintegral_abs_pow_ne_top {ρ : Measure ℝ} {M : ℝ} (h : HasFactorialMomentBound ρ M)
    (n : ℕ) : ∫⁻ x, ENNReal.ofReal (|x| ^ n) ∂ρ ≠ ⊤ :=
  ne_top_of_le_ne_top ENNReal.ofReal_ne_top (h n)

theorem integrable_pow_of_factorialMomentBound {ρ : Measure ℝ} {M : ℝ}
    (h : HasFactorialMomentBound ρ M) (n : ℕ) : Integrable (fun x : ℝ => x ^ n) ρ := by
  refine ⟨(measurable_id.pow_const n).aestronglyMeasurable, ?_⟩
  rw [hasFiniteIntegral_iff_enorm]
  have hle : ∀ x : ℝ, ‖x ^ n‖ₑ = ENNReal.ofReal (|x| ^ n) := by
    intro x
    rw [← Real.enorm_eq_ofReal (by positivity), ← abs_pow]
    simp
  simp_rw [hle]
  exact lt_of_le_of_ne le_top (lintegral_abs_pow_ne_top h n)

theorem integrable_abs_pow_of_factorialMomentBound {ρ : Measure ℝ} {M : ℝ}
    (h : HasFactorialMomentBound ρ M) (n : ℕ) :
    Integrable (fun x : ℝ => |x| ^ n) ρ := by
  have := integrable_pow_of_factorialMomentBound h n
  simpa [abs_pow] using this.abs

theorem integral_abs_pow_le {ρ : Measure ℝ} {M : ℝ} (hM : 0 ≤ M)
    (h : HasFactorialMomentBound ρ M) (n : ℕ) :
    ∫ x : ℝ, |x| ^ n ∂ρ ≤ (Nat.factorial n : ℝ) * M ^ n := by
  have hnn : 0 ≤ᵐ[ρ] fun x : ℝ => |x| ^ n := Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun x => by positivity
  have hlint : ENNReal.ofReal (∫ x : ℝ, |x| ^ n ∂ρ) = ∫⁻ x, ENNReal.ofReal (|x| ^ n) ∂ρ :=
    ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal (integrable_abs_pow_of_factorialMomentBound h n) hnn
  have hle : ENNReal.ofReal (∫ x : ℝ, |x| ^ n ∂ρ) ≤
      ENNReal.ofReal ((Nat.factorial n : ℝ) * M ^ n) := by
    rw [hlint]
    exact h n
  exact (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal_iff (by positivity)).mp hle

/-- **Exponential window from factorial moments.**  A factorial-geometric moment bound makes every
exponential with small enough rate integrable. -/
theorem integrable_exp_mul_of_factorialMomentBound {ρ : Measure ℝ} {M : ℝ} (hM : 0 < M)
    (h : HasFactorialMomentBound ρ M) {t : ℝ} (ht : |t| * M < 1) :
    Integrable (fun x : ℝ => Real.exp (t * x)) ρ := by
  set q : ℝ := |t| * M with hq
  have hq0 : 0 ≤ q := by positivity
  have hsummable : Summable fun n : ℕ => q ^ n := summable_geometric_of_lt_one hq0 ht
  have hbound : ∀ n : ℕ, ∫⁻ x, ENNReal.ofReal ((|t| * |x|) ^ n / (Nat.factorial n : ℝ)) ∂ρ ≤
      ENNReal.ofReal (q ^ n) := by
    intro n
    have hfac : (0 : ℝ) < (Nat.factorial n : ℝ) := by
      exact_mod_cast Nat.factorial_pos n
    have hrw : ∀ x : ℝ, ENNReal.ofReal ((|t| * |x|) ^ n / (Nat.factorial n : ℝ)) =
        ENNReal.ofReal (|t| ^ n / (Nat.factorial n : ℝ)) * ENNReal.ofReal (|x| ^ n) := by
      intro x
      rw [← ENNReal.ofReal_mul (by positivity)]
      congr 1
      rw [mul_pow]
      field_simp
    simp_rw [hrw]
    rw [lintegral_const_mul' _ _ ENNReal.ofReal_ne_top]
    refine le_trans (mul_le_mul' le_rfl (h n)) ?_
    rw [← ENNReal.ofReal_mul (by positivity)]
    refine ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal (le_of_eq ?_)
    rw [hq, mul_pow]
    field_simp
  have hfinite : ∫⁻ x, ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp (|t| * |x|)) ∂ρ ≤
      ENNReal.ofReal (1 - q)⁻¹ := by
    have hseries : ∀ x : ℝ, ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp (|t| * |x|)) =
        ∑' n : ℕ, ENNReal.ofReal ((|t| * |x|) ^ n / (Nat.factorial n : ℝ)) := by
      intro x
      have hexp : Real.exp (|t| * |x|) =
          ∑' n : ℕ, (|t| * |x|) ^ n / (Nat.factorial n : ℝ) := by
        rw [Real.exp_eq_exp_ℝ, NormedSpace.exp_eq_tsum_div]
      rw [hexp]
      refine ENNReal.ofReal_tsum_of_nonneg (fun n => by positivity) ?_
      have := Real.summable_pow_div_factorial (|t| * |x|)
      simpa using this
    simp_rw [hseries]
    have hswap := lintegral_tsum (μ := ρ)
      (f := fun (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) => ENNReal.ofReal ((|t| * |x|) ^ n / (Nat.factorial n : ℝ)))
      (fun n => (ENNReal.measurable_ofReal.comp
        (((measurable_const.mul measurable_id.abs).pow_const n).div_const _)).aemeasurable)

import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.Sieve.CircleDistance

/-!
# The Gram row of a family separated on the circle

A family of frequencies separated by `δ` in `ℝ/ℤ` has harmonic Gram rows:

`∑_{t ≠ r} ‖λ_t - λ_r‖^{-1} ≤ 2 δ^{-1} ∑_{1 ≤ k ≤ M} k^{-1}`,  `M ≥ (2δ)^{-1}`.

Unlike the real-line estimate of `SeparatedRowSum.lean`, the index ordering says nothing here — on
the circle the frequencies may wrap — so the count is made by *level* instead.  Reducing each
`λ_t - λ_r` modulo one gives an offset in `[-1/2, 1/2]` whose absolute value lies in some band
`[kδ, (k+1)δ)`.  Two frequencies in the same band on the same side of zero have offsets differing by
less than `δ`, hence lie within `δ` of each other on the circle (`toIntDist_sub_lt`), contradicting
the separation hypothesis.  So the level–side pair is injective, at most two frequencies occupy each
level, and every level is at most `(2δ)^{-1}` because the offsets never exceed `1/2`.

The resulting `δ^{-1} log δ^{-1}` is the honest ceiling of the absolute-value method, matching the
real-line bound: no ordering is used, only the separation.
-/

namespace RHTower.Sieve

open Finset

/-- The representative of a real number modulo one, taken in `[-1/2, 1/2]`. -/
noncomputable def reduce (x : ℝ) : ℝ := x - (round x : ℝ)

theorem toIntDist_eq_abs_reduce (x : ℝ) : toIntDist x = |reduce x| := rfl

/-- The band of a circle distance: the number of full `δ` steps it contains. -/
noncomputable def levelOf (δ x : ℝ) : ℕ := ⌊|reduce x| / δ⌋₊

/-- A separated frequency sits at a positive level. -/
theorem one_le_levelOf {δ x : ℝ} (hδ0 : 0 < δ) (hx : δ ≤ toIntDist x) : 1 ≤ levelOf δ x := by
  refine Nat.le_floor ?_
  rw [Nat.cast_one, le_div_iff₀ hδ0, one_mul]
  exact hx

/-- The level is a lower bound for the circle distance. -/
theorem levelOf_mul_le {δ x : ℝ} (hδ0 : 0 < δ) : (levelOf δ x : ℝ) * δ ≤ toIntDist x := by
  have hnn : (0 : ℝ) ≤ |reduce x| / δ := by positivity
  have h := Nat.floor_le hnn
  rw [le_div_iff₀ hδ0] at h
  exact h

/-- The circle distance is below the next band. -/
theorem lt_levelOf_succ_mul {δ x : ℝ} (hδ0 : 0 < δ) :
    toIntDist x < ((levelOf δ x : ℝ) + 1) * δ := by
  have h := Nat.lt_floor_add_one (|reduce x| / δ)
  rw [div_lt_iff₀ hδ0] at h
  exact h

/-- Offsets never exceed a half, so levels never exceed `(2δ)^{-1}`. -/
theorem levelOf_le {δ x : ℝ} (hδ0 : 0 < δ) {M : ℕ} (hM : 1 / (2 * δ) ≤ (M : ℝ)) :
    levelOf δ x ≤ M := by
  have hhalf : |reduce x| ≤ 1 / 2 := toIntDist_le_half x
  have hprod : 1 / (2 * δ) * δ = 1 / 2 := by field_simp
  have h1 : 1 / (2 * δ) * δ ≤ (M : ℝ) * δ := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hM (le_of_lt hδ0)
  rw [hprod] at h1
  have hbound : |reduce x| / δ ≤ (M : ℝ) := by
    rw [div_le_iff₀ hδ0]
    linarith
  calc levelOf δ x = ⌊|reduce x| / δ⌋₊ := rfl
    _ ≤ ⌊(M : ℝ)⌋₊ := Nat.floor_le_floor hbound
    _ = M := Nat.floor_natCast M

/-- **The Gram row of a `δ`-separated family on the circle is harmonic.** -/
theorem circle_row_sum_le {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] (s : Finset ι) (lam : ι → ℝ) {δ : ℝ}
    (hδ0 : 0 < δ) (hδ : δ ≤ 1 / 2)
    (hsep : ∀ a ∈ s, ∀ b ∈ s, a ≠ b → δ ≤ toIntDist (lam b - lam a))
    {r : ι} (hr : r ∈ s) {M : ℕ} (hM : 1 / (2 * δ) ≤ (M : ℝ)) :
    ∑ t ∈ s.erase r, 1 / toIntDist (lam t - lam r)
      ≤ (2 / δ) * ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 M, 1 / (k : ℝ) := by
  classical
  set F : ι → ℕ × Bool :=
    fun t => (levelOf δ (lam t - lam r), decide (0 ≤ reduce (lam t - lam r))) with hF
  have hsep' : ∀ t ∈ s.erase r, δ ≤ toIntDist (lam t - lam r) := by
    intro t ht
    have ht' := Finset.mem_erase.mp ht
    exact hsep r hr t ht'.2 (Ne.symm ht'.1)
  -- termwise: the reciprocal distance is at most `δ⁻¹` times the reciprocal level
  have hterm : ∀ t ∈ s.erase r,
      1 / toIntDist (lam t - lam r) ≤ (1 / δ) * (1 / ((F t).1 : ℝ)) := by
    intro t ht
    have hs := hsep' t ht
    have hlev1 : 1 ≤ levelOf δ (lam t - lam r) := one_le_levelOf hδ0 hs
    have hlevR : (1 : ℝ) ≤ (levelOf δ (lam t - lam r) : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hlev1
    have hpos : (0 : ℝ) < (levelOf δ (lam t - lam r) : ℝ) * δ := by positivity
    have hle := levelOf_mul_le (δ := δ) (x := lam t - lam r) hδ0
    have hmain := one_div_le_one_div_of_le hpos hle
    have hval : 1 / ((levelOf δ (lam t - lam r) : ℝ) * δ)
        = (1 / δ) * (1 / (levelOf δ (lam t - lam r) : ℝ)) := by
      field_simp
    rw [hval] at hmain
    exact hmain
  -- the level–side pair separates the frequencies
  have hinj : ∀ a ∈ s.erase r, ∀ b ∈ s.erase r, F a = F b → a = b := by
    intro a ha b hb hab
    by_contra hne
    simp only [hF, Prod.mk.injEq, decide_eq_decide] at hab
    obtain ⟨hlev, hside⟩ := hab
    have hla := levelOf_mul_le (δ := δ) (x := lam a - lam r) hδ0
    have hlb := levelOf_mul_le (δ := δ) (x := lam b - lam r) hδ0
    have hua := lt_levelOf_succ_mul (δ := δ) (x := lam a - lam r) hδ0
    have hub := lt_levelOf_succ_mul (δ := δ) (x := lam b - lam r) hδ0
    rw [hlev] at hla hua

import Mathlib.NumberTheory.SumPrimeReciprocals

/-!
# Critical dilation absolute-contraction obstruction

The exact Möbius--Laplace Lambert law has critical dilation weight `k^(-1/2)`.  Its restriction to
prime indices is already nonsummable.  More sharply, no correction can have summable critical
prime mass simultaneously with the coefficient obtained by adding the uncorrected prime tail.

This closes absolute-value Neumann-series attacks on the critical renewal equation.  Any viable
dilation argument must retain conditional signed cancellation of the distinguished Möbius
solution.
-/

open Complex Filter
open scoped Topology

namespace RHTower

noncomputable section

/-- Prime power mass is nonsummable throughout the closed exponent range `[-1, +infinity)`.
This is the obstruction range relevant to critical dilation weights. -/
theorem not_summable_primeRpow_of_negOne_le {r : ℝ} (hr : -1 ≤ r) :
    ¬ Summable (fun p : Nat.Primes => (p : ℝ) ^ r) := by
  rw [Nat.Primes.summable_rpow]
  exact not_lt_of_ge hr

/-- **Sharp absolute-correction obstruction.**  At every prime-power exponent `r >= -1`, a
correction and the coefficient obtained by adding the constant prime tail cannot both have
summable weighted norm. -/
theorem no_simultaneous_summable_primeRpowCorrection
    (b : Nat.Primes → ℂ) {r : ℝ} (hr : -1 ≤ r) :
    ¬ (Summable (fun p : Nat.Primes => ‖b p‖ * (p : ℝ) ^ r) ∧
       Summable (fun p : Nat.Primes => ‖1 + b p‖ * (p : ℝ) ^ r)) := by
  rintro ⟨hb, hcorrected⟩
  apply not_summable_primeRpow_of_negOne_le hr
  have hmajor := hb.add hcorrected
  refine Summable.of_nonneg_of_le (fun p => by positivity) (fun p => ?_) hmajor
  have htriangle : (1 : ℝ) ≤ ‖b p‖ + ‖1 + b p‖ := by
    have h := norm_sub_le (1 + b p) (b p)
    simpa [add_comm] using h
  have hweight : 0 ≤ (p : ℝ) ^ r := by positivity
  calc
    (p : ℝ) ^ r = 1 * (p : ℝ) ^ r := by ring
    _ ≤ (‖b p‖ + ‖1 + b p‖) * (p : ℝ) ^ r :=
      mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right htriangle hweight
    _ = ‖b p‖ * (p : ℝ) ^ r + ‖1 + b p‖ * (p : ℝ) ^ r := by ring

/-- The critical prime dilation mass `sum_p p^(-1/2)` is not summable. -/
theorem not_summable_primeCriticalDilationWeight :
    ¬ Summable (fun p : Nat.Primes => (p : ℝ) ^ (-(1 / 2 : ℝ))) :=
  not_summable_primeRpow_of_negOne_le (by norm_num)

/-- No absolutely controlled infinite correction can turn the critical constant prime tail into
an absolutely summable contraction tail. -/
theorem no_simultaneous_summable_primeCriticalDilationCorrection
    (b : Nat.Primes → ℂ) :
    ¬ (Summable (fun p : Nat.Primes =>
          ‖b p‖ * (p : ℝ) ^ (-(1 / 2 : ℝ))) ∧
       Summable (fun p : Nat.Primes =>
          ‖1 + b p‖ * (p : ℝ) ^ (-(1 / 2 : ℝ)))) :=
  no_simultaneous_summable_primeRpowCorrection b (by norm_num)

/-- Finite prime corrections are a fortiori impossible: an eventually zero correction leaves the
coefficient equal to one on a cofinite set of primes. -/
theorem not_summable_primeCriticalDilationCorrection_of_eventually_zero
    (b : Nat.Primes → ℂ) (hb : b =ᶠ[cofinite] 0) :
    ¬ Summable (fun p : Nat.Primes =>
      ‖1 + b p‖ * (p : ℝ) ^ (-(1 / 2 : ℝ))) := by
  intro hcorrected
  apply not_summable_primeCriticalDilationWeight
  apply hcorrected.congr_cofinite
  filter_upwards [hb] with p hp
  simp [hp]

/-- Canonical embedding of a prime index into the positive dilation semigroup. -/
def primeAsPositiveDilation (p : Nat.Primes) : ℕ+ :=
  ⟨p, p.property.pos⟩

/-- The concrete critical renewal weights are nonsummable even after restriction to prime
dilations.  Absolute convergence of the actual renewal series therefore comes from transform-value
cancellation and cannot be bounded by the weights alone. -/
theorem not_summable_prime_mobiusLaplaceCriticalRenewalWeight :
    ¬ Summable (fun p : Nat.Primes =>
      mobiusLaplaceCriticalRenewalWeight (primeAsPositiveDilation p)) := by
  simpa [mobiusLaplaceCriticalRenewalWeight_eq_rpow] using!
    not_summable_primeCriticalDilationWeight

end

end RHTower

/-!
# Dilation-universal graded Born KMS phase beyond the Gibbs wall

The Born parity supertrace converges throughout the positive high-temperature strip where the
ungraded Gibbs trace diverges.  Exact dilation covariance transports that graded phase through
every positive dilation channel: each dilated supertrace is summable, strictly positive, and is
the prescribed KMS multiple of the original graded trace.
-/

namespace RHTower

noncomputable section

/-- **Dilation-universal graded wall law.**  Every positive dilation preserves the convergent,
positive, exactly covariant graded trace throughout `0 < β ≤ 2`, even though the ungraded Gibbs
trace diverges there. -/
theorem dilatedBornSuperKMS_beyond_ungraded_wall
    {β : ℝ} (hβ0 : 0 < β) (hβ2 : β ≤ 2)
    {k : ℕ} (hk : 0 < k) :
    Summable (dilatedBornSupertraceTerm k β) ∧
      ¬ Summable (fun n : ℕ => ((n : ℝ) + 1) ^ (-(β / 2))) ∧
      (∑' n : ℕ, dilatedBornSupertraceTerm k β n) =
        (k : ℝ) ^ (-(β / 2)) * bornSupertrace β ∧
      0 < ∑' n : ℕ, dilatedBornSupertraceTerm k β n := by
  have hwall := gradedOrder_beyond_wall hβ0 hβ2
  have hsum : Summable (dilatedBornSupertraceTerm k β) := by
    exact (hwall.1.mul_left ((k : ℝ) ^ (-(β / 2)))).congr
      (fun n => (dilatedBornSupertraceTerm_eq hk β n).symm)
  have hvalue := tsum_dilatedBornSupertraceTerm hk β
  refine ⟨hsum, hwall.2, hvalue, ?_⟩
  rw [hvalue]
  exact mul_pos (Real.rpow_pos_of_pos (by exact_mod_cast hk) _) (bornSupertrace_pos hβ0)

/-- Odd dilation channels additionally preserve the parity grading pointwise while remaining in
the same beyond-wall phase. -/
theorem oddDilatedBornSuperKMS_beyond_ungraded_wall
    {β : ℝ} (hβ0 : 0 < β) (hβ2 : β ≤ 2)
    {k : ℕ} (hk : Odd k) :
    (∀ n : ℕ, ((-1 : ℝ)) ^ (k * n) = (-1) ^ n) ∧
      Summable (dilatedBornSupertraceTerm k β) ∧
      ¬ Summable (fun n : ℕ => ((n : ℝ) + 1) ^ (-(β / 2))) ∧
      0 < ∑' n : ℕ, dilatedBornSupertraceTerm k β n := by
  have hk0 : 0 < k := hk.pos
  have hphase := dilatedBornSuperKMS_beyond_ungraded_wall hβ0 hβ2 hk0
  exact ⟨gradedSign_mul_odd hk, hphase.1, hphase.2.1, hphase.2.2.2⟩

end

end RHTower

/-!
# Summable Euler Calkin injectivity

The finite scaled-shell separation theorem extends to every nonzero absolutely summable family at
strictly increasing scales. Consequently no nonzero operator-norm convergent additive series of
positive Euler metric corners becomes compact. The result is proved on ambient `L²(ℝ)`, restricted
to the actual even Sonin carrier, and transported to the concrete archimedean
Hardy--Titchmarsh line.

This theorem concerns `ℓ¹` additive renormalizations. It does not cover conditionally summed Euler
series, multiplicative phase-ratio products, or regulator-dependent all-place limits.
-/

noncomputable section

open MeasureTheory Set
open Filter Topology
open scoped InnerProduct InnerProductSpace

namespace RHTower

theorem norm_dilationSum_le_two (r : ℝ) (hr : 1 < r) :
    ‖dilationSum r hr‖ ≤ 2 := by
  apply (dilationSum r hr).opNorm_le_bound (by norm_num)
  intro f
  rw [dilationSum_apply]
  calc
    ‖dilation r (zero_lt_one.trans hr) f +
        dilation r⁻¹ (inv_pos.mpr (zero_lt_one.trans hr)) f‖
        ≤ ‖dilation r (zero_lt_one.trans hr) f‖ +
          ‖dilation r⁻¹ (inv_pos.mpr (zero_lt_one.trans hr)) f‖ := norm_add_le _ _
    _ = 2 * ‖f‖ := by
      rw [(dilation r (zero_lt_one.trans hr)).norm_map,
        (dilation r⁻¹ (inv_pos.mpr (zero_lt_one.trans hr))).norm_map]
      ring

theorem summable_smul_dilationSum
    (r : ℕ → ℝ) (hr : ∀ j, 1 < r j) (c : ℕ → ℂ)
    (hc : Summable fun j => ‖c j‖) :
    Summable fun j => c j • dilationSum (r j) (hr j) := by
  apply Summable.of_norm_bounded (Summable.mul_left 2 hc)
  intro j
  calc
    ‖c j • dilationSum (r j) (hr j)‖
        ≤ ‖c j‖ * ‖dilationSum (r j) (hr j)‖ :=
          ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_smul_le _ _
    _ ≤ ‖c j‖ * 2 := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left
      (norm_dilationSum_le_two (r j) (hr j)) (norm_nonneg _)
    _ = 2 * ‖c j‖ := by ring

/-- The operator-norm convergent symmetric-dilation series. -/
def summableDilationCombination
    (r : ℕ → ℝ) (hr : ∀ j, 1 < r j) (c : ℕ → ℂ) :
    SoninL2 →L[ℂ] SoninL2 :=
  ∑' j, c j • dilationSum (r j) (hr j)

theorem exists_strictMono_separatingShellUpper
    {a : ℝ} (r : ℕ → ℝ) (hr : ∀ j, 1 < r j) (hmono : StrictMono r)
    (k : ℕ) (ha : 0 < a) :
    ∃ b : ℝ, a < b ∧ b ≤ r k * a ∧
      ∀ j, k < j → b * r k < a * r j := by
  have hk0 : 0 < r k := zero_lt_one.trans (hr k)
  have hnext : r k < r (k + 1) := hmono (Nat.lt_succ_self k)
  let u : ℝ := min (r k * a) (a * r (k + 1) / r k)
  have hau : a < u := by
    rw [lt_min_iff]
    constructor
    · nlinarith [hr k]
    · rw [lt_div_iff₀ hk0]
      nlinarith
  let b : ℝ := (a + u) / 2
  have hab : a < b := by dsimp [b]; linarith
  have hbu : b < u := by dsimp [b]; linarith
  refine ⟨b, hab, hbu.le.trans (min_le_left _ _), ?_⟩
  intro j hkj
  have hsucc : k + 1 ≤ j := Nat.succ_le_iff.mpr hkj
  have hscale : r (k + 1) ≤ r j := hmono.monotone hsucc
  have hub : u ≤ a * r (k + 1) / r k := min_le_right _ _
  have hbnext : b * r k < a * r (k + 1) := by
    rw [← lt_div_iff₀ hk0]
    exact hbu.trans_le hub
  nlinarith

theorem scaledEvenShellCutoff_summableDilationCombination_apply
    {a b : ℝ} (r : ℕ → ℝ) (hr : ∀ j, 1 < r j)
    (c : ℕ → ℂ) (hc : Summable fun j => ‖c j‖)
    (k : ℕ) (hmin : ∀ j, j < k → c j = 0)
    (ha : 0 < a) (hab : a < b) (hba : b ≤ r k * a)

# Shifted Towers Do Not Fix The T0 Tail Class

- **ID:** shifted-towers-do-not-fix-t0-tail-class
- **Stage:** 3-formalized
- **Type:** THEOREM (paper)
- **Source:** docs/consolidated/gpt/proof-route.md, `T_0` infinite / shifted finite towers
- **Statement:** Finiteness of every positive shifted moment is compatible with many incompatible divergence rates for the unshifted mass `T_0`. Therefore the shifted proof route does not supply a canonical `T_0` regularization rate.

## Goal

Block a Tauberian false repair of the invalid unshifted `T_0` tower. Once the route shifts away from `T_0`, the finiteness of the shifted tower alone does not identify whether the missing `T_0` divergence is logarithmic, linear, stretched-exponential in a cutoff, or another admissible near-zero tail class.

## Gates

- [x] 0 -> 1 in-progress: well-posed, source-pure, attack idea
- [x] 1 -> 2 fully-proven: complete paper proof, `[PROVED HERE]`, no open dependency
- [x] 2 -> 3 formalized: `RHTower/ShiftedTowerTailClasses.lean`, targeted build green, axiom audit clean
- [ ] 3 -> 4 publication-ready: standalone note if needed

## Proof

[PROVED HERE]

Let `(a_n)_{n>=1}` be positive and define a reciprocal measure

```text
mu = sum_{n>=1} a_n delta_{exp(-n)}.
```

Then

```text
T_0 = sum_n a_n,
T_k = sum_n a_n exp(-kn),  k>=1.
```

If

```text
sum_n a_n = infinity
```

but

```text
sum_n a_n exp(-kn) < infinity  for every k>=1,
```

then `T_0` is infinite while every shifted positive moment is finite.

The condition allows many incompatible `T_0` divergence classes. For example:

```text
a_n = 1/n          gives T_0(N) ~ log N,
a_n = 1            gives T_0(N) = N,
a_n = exp(sqrt n)  gives stretched-exponential T_0(N),
```

and in all three cases `sum_n a_n exp(-kn)<infinity` for every `k>=1`.

By contrast, the control case

```text
a_n = exp(n)
```

already makes `T_1=sum_n exp(n) exp(-n)=sum_n 1` diverge, so it is outside the shifted finite tower regime.

Thus the shifted finite tower condition separates admissible from too-large near-zero mass, but it does not choose one admissible `T_0` divergence rate. Any proof route that reinstates `T_0` by a cutoff, finite part, or Tauberian normalization must import an additional source theorem specifying the near-zero tail class.

three weights satisfy the shifted-finite condition, yet their unshifted partial sums are pairwise
separated by a vanishing ratio, so the shifted tower cannot select one divergence class.

## 3. What this makes the next question

Not "construct the energy" — that is the whole programme. The sharper question, and the one that can
be settled either way:

> **Is `hdetects` obstructed?** The parent card's own falsifier list contains
> *"Orthogonal Hilbert completion before incidence makes the scalar quotient seminorm zero"*, and the
> roadmap card states *"unweighted infinite-ray Hilbert augmentation has zero quotient seminorm"*.
> If the natural candidate energy is the Hilbert seminorm of the Meyer quotient and that seminorm
> vanishes identically, then `energy ≡ 0` and `hdetects` fails as badly as possible.

Two outcomes, both worth having:

- **a no-go** — no energy with the required equivariance and locality can detect zero. That would be
  the **first proved death of a quadratic route** in this corpus. Every quadratic route so far has
  died unbuilt, i.e. of nobody managing; a proof that it *cannot* be built is different in kind and
  would settle the lane.
- **a construction constraint** — the obstruction is only for the *unweighted* completion, and the
  weight/suspension prescription evades it. Then the prescription "nuclear cohomology before Hilbert
  completion" is not stylistic but forced, and one can say exactly which weights survive.

## 4. The no-go question is settled: it is not a no-go, it is a weight criterion

Section 3 asked whether `hdetects` is obstructed, given the corpus's own
`eq_zero_of_infinite_subgroup_leftInvariant_summable_normSq`
(`HTGeometry/OrbitQuotientLiftNoGo.lean`): a square-summable regular vector invariant under an
infinite subgroup is zero, so the invariants of `l^2(G)` under an infinite `H` are `{0}` and the
object one wants is **absent from the completion**, not merely small in it.

Answer: that obstruction is entirely an artifact of the *unweighted* norm, and the repair is sharp.
Formalized in `HTGeometry/WeightedOrbitInvariantExistence.lean`, axiom-clean
`[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`:

```text
summable_weight_orbit_of_invariant
    (H : Subgroup G) (w : G → ℝ) (f : G → E)
    (hsum : Summable fun g => w g * ‖f g‖ ^ 2)
    (hinv : ∀ h : H, ∀ y, f (h.1 * y) = f y)
    {x : G} (hx : f x ≠ 0) :
    Summable fun h : H => w (h.1 * x)

exists_nonzero_invariant_of_summable_weight_orbit
    (H : Subgroup G) (w : G → ℝ) (x : G) (v : E)
    (horb : Summable fun h : H => w (h.1 * x)) :
    ∃ f, f x = v ∧ (∀ h : H, ∀ y, f (h.1 * y) = f y) ∧ Summable fun g => w g * ‖f g‖ ^ 2

eq_zero_of_infinite_subgroup_invariant_unweighted   -- the corpus no-go, as the case w ≡ 1
```

**The dichotomy is exact.** The invariants of the weighted completion are controlled by one scalar
per orbit, the pushforward weight `W(H·x) = sum_(h in H) w(h·x)`: a nonzero invariant vector forces
`W(H·x) < ∞` wherever it does not vanish, and conversely `W(H·x) < ∞` on a single orbit already
produces one — the indicator of that orbit. Taking `w ≡ 1` gives back the no-go, because
`sum_(h in H) 1` diverges for infinite `H`. So the no-go is precisely the statement that the constant
weight is not orbit-summable, and nothing more.

`deninger-source-native-arithmetic-cohomology-roadmap.md` prescribes *"Smooth suspension and unit
augmentation must therefore precede Hilbert completion … Nuclear cohomology must be formed first"*,
and the parent card lists as a falsifier *"Orthogonal Hilbert completion before incidence makes the
scalar quotient seminorm zero."* Both are correct, and both were stated as **methodological
warnings**. They now have a quantitative form:

> Complete against a weight that is summable along the orbits of the period subgroup, and the
> invariants survive. Complete against the unweighted norm, and they are annihilated. There is no
> third case.

## 2026-08-06 (fifth pass) — the reading law on an enlarged domain

The lane is closed as a criterion (fourth pass), but the *reader* was still tied to `ell^1`. This pass
enlarges its domain, which is what a producer actually needs: a source field that agrees with the
first wall up to a non-summable but pointwise small error.

### Negligible fields

Call `b` *negligible* against `h` when for every `ε > 0` there is a finite set off which
`‖b i‖ ≤ ε · h i`. Negligible fields need not be summable and summable fields need not be
negligible — the classes are incomparable. Over the primes with `h(p) = 1/p`, negligible means
`b(p) = o(1/p)` with an explicit depth threshold, and this catches non-summable examples: `∑_p 1/p`
diverges like `log log x`, so `b(p) = 1/(p log log p)` is not summable while `p · b(p) → 0`.

`[PROVED HERE]` Negligible fields are invisible to cofinal averaging. Once a stage vanishes on the
finite exceptional set, the bound `mu_N(i) ‖b(i)‖ ≤ ε · (mu_N(i) h(i))` holds at *every* index, so the
unit reference mass gives `‖A_N(b)‖ ≤ ε` directly — no convergence of `b` is used. Summability of the
stage terms at a fixed `N`, where escape has not yet happened, comes from majorizing by
`mu_N h + indicator(s)·mu_N‖b‖`.

Hence the residue is read modulo `ell^1 + negligible`:

`HasReferenceResidueMod h a c := ∃ b₁ b₂, Summable b₁ ∧ IsCofinitelyNegligible h b₂ ∧
   a - c h = b₁ + b₂`

and `tendsto_profileAverage_mod` gives `A_N(a) → c` on that larger domain, with uniqueness from the
existence of a single profile (`HasReferenceResidueMod.unique_of_profile`).

### Robust criterion

`[PROVED HERE]` The threshold test transfers to any producer field: if `a - W_t` is summable or
`o(1/p)`, then `a` carries the same oriented residue, so a frequent sub-quantum bound on `a`'s own
averages forces `t = 0`
(`eq_zero_of_frequently_abs_re_profileAverage_le_of_negligible_sub`), and

`riemannHypothesis_of_frequently_negligible_producer`

closes RH from producer fields that need never equal the first-wall field exactly.

The first pass claimed the restarted Euler sieve was "one instance" of the universal reading law but

The equivalence uses this theorem together with the following elementary lemma. If a zero-free entire function `F` satisfies (1), write `F=exp(g)` with `g` entire. Then

## Literature boundary

For a jointly entire one-sided periodic heat orbit, the multiplicative anchor has `log M(r)=o((log r)^2)`. Therefore its zero divisor has `n(r)=o(log r)`. ## Exact statement

Let `a_N : ℕ → ℝ` be nonnegative decreasing summable sequences. If, for every `r ≥ 0`,
`Σ_k a_N(k)^(2r+2) → normalizedPrimeArchMoment r`, then `Σ_k a_N(k) → +∞`.
Consequently no uniformly root-nuclear family, even with changing aperture, dimension,
carrier or mixing, can land on all completed Xi moments. Operator half-normalization uses
the sequence repeating each singular value twice; no reflection copy or multiplicity is lost.

Checked locks: `GammaSewnPluckerGlobalMeanMomentNoGo` excludes exact fixed-carrier landing;
`SoninRegularizedMomentWeldNoGo` handles its literal regularized cofinal family.
Surviving edge addressed here: approximate moment landing with a uniformly bounded root budget.
This does not exclude families with diverging root budget or prove an arithmetic selector.

## Proof

1. Suppose root budgets do not tend to infinity. Pass to a cofinal subsequence with
   `Σ a_N ≤ C`. Nonnegativity implies `C ≥ 0` and monotonicity gives
   `a_N(k) ≤ C/(k+1)`.
2. Product compactness of `[0,C]^ℕ` gives a pointwise convergent sub-subsequence `a_N → b`.
   Finite sums pass to the limit: `b ≥ 0`, `b` decreases, and `Σ b ≤ C`.
3. For every `r`, the common summable majorant
   `C^(2r) * (C/(k+1))²` dominates `a_N(k)^(2r+2)`.
   Dominated convergence therefore gives exact squared-power moments for `b`.
4. Its positive Hankel representation implies RH via the existing complete prime--Gamma
   moment criterion. Under this internally derived RH, existing Xi moment identification
   and ordered moment determinacy identify `b` with the full multiplicity-exact ordered Xi
   reciprocal sequence. That sequence is not summable. Contradiction.

Positive survivor: accurate cofinal moment landing must pay an unbounded, eventually
arbitrarily large root budget, not merely change aperture. No rate claimed.

Finite consequence: for each budget `C`, some degree `n` separates every admissible
sequence from the Xi moments by at least `1/(n+1)` in one of its first `n+1` moments.
Otherwise choose a sequence for each `n` approximating those moments more closely;
every fixed moment then converges and steps 1--4 contradict the common budget.
The degree is existential; this is not a computed numerical certificate.

Fixed-source consequence: if `A_N = B_N A C_N` with nuclear `A`, then
`Σ s_k(A_N) ≤ ||B_N|| ||C_N|| Σ s_k(A)`. Exact asymptotic half-normalized Xi
energy moments therefore force `||B_N|| ||C_N|| → ∞`. In particular bounded
stage-dependent mixing of the actual C1 root cannot evade the firewall.

# The Euler bound for a bounded multiplicative Dirichlet series

The damping estimate of `EulerDamping.lean` bounds a *finite* Euler product over squarefree smooth
integers.  Halász's method needs the same bound for the whole Dirichlet series of a multiplicative
function, prime powers included:

`‖∑_n f(n) n^{-s}‖ ≤ exp(∑_p Re(f(p) p^{-s}) + 5/2)`  for `Re s > 1`, `|f| ≤ 1`.

Each local factor `∑_e f(p^e) p^{-es}` is `1 + f(p)p^{-s}` plus a tail of size at most `2p^{-2Re s}`,
so `‖1 + z‖ ≤ exp(Re z + ‖z‖²)` still applies after the tail is folded into the exponent.  The
resulting per-prime excess is summable against `∑_p p^{-2}`, whose value stays below `49/100`, so the
whole prime-power contribution costs one absolute constant.

The gain over the squarefree proxy is that the left side is now the actual Dirichlet series, so the
bound composes with Perron inversion.
-/

/-- The twisted summand `n ↦ f n · n^{-s}` of a Dirichlet series. -/
noncomputable def twistedSummand (f : ℕ → ℂ) (s : ℂ) (n : ℕ) : ℂ :=
  f n * (n : ℂ) ^ (-s)

section

variable {f : ℕ → ℂ} {s : ℂ}

theorem twistedSummand_zero (hs : s ≠ 0) : twistedSummand f s 0 = 0 := by
  rw [twistedSummand, Nat.cast_zero, Complex.zero_cpow (neg_ne_zero.mpr hs), mul_zero]

theorem twistedSummand_one (hf1 : f 1 = 1) : twistedSummand f s 1 = 1 := by
  rw [twistedSummand, hf1, Nat.cast_one, Complex.one_cpow, mul_one]

theorem natCast_cpow_mul (m n : ℕ) :
    ((m * n : ℕ) : ℂ) ^ (-s) = ((m : ℕ) : ℂ) ^ (-s) * ((n : ℕ) : ℂ) ^ (-s) := by
  have h : ((m * n : ℕ) : ℂ) = (((m : ℝ) : ℂ)) * (((n : ℝ) : ℂ)) := by
    push_cast
    ring
  rw [h, Complex.mul_cpow_ofReal_nonneg m.cast_nonneg n.cast_nonneg,
    Complex.ofReal_natCast, Complex.ofReal_natCast]

theorem twistedSummand_mul
    (hmul : ∀ {m n : ℕ}, Nat.Coprime m n → f (m * n) = f m * f n)
    {m n : ℕ} (h : Nat.Coprime m n) :
    twistedSummand f s (m * n) = twistedSummand f s m * twistedSummand f s n := by
  rw [twistedSummand, twistedSummand, twistedSummand, hmul h, natCast_cpow_mul]
  ring

theorem norm_twistedSummand_le (hbdd : ∀ n, ‖f n‖ ≤ 1) {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) :
    ‖twistedSummand f s n‖ ≤ ((n : ℝ)) ^ (-s.re) := by
  have h1 : ‖((n : ℕ) : ℂ) ^ (-s)‖ = ((n : ℝ)) ^ (-s.re) := by
    rw [Complex.norm_natCast_cpow_of_pos hn, Complex.neg_re]
  rw [twistedSummand, norm_mul, h1]
  exact mul_le_of_le_one_left (Real.rpow_nonneg (Nat.cast_nonneg n) _) (hbdd n)

theorem summable_nat_rpow_neg {σ : ℝ} (hσ : 1 < σ) :
    Summable (fun n : ℕ => ((n : ℝ)) ^ (-σ)) := by
  refine (Real.summable_nat_rpow_inv.mpr hσ).congr fun n => ?_
  rw [Real.rpow_neg (Nat.cast_nonneg n)]

theorem summable_norm_twistedSummand (hbdd : ∀ n, ‖f n‖ ≤ 1) (hs : 1 < s.re) :
    Summable (fun n : ℕ => ‖twistedSummand f s n‖) := by
  refine (summable_nat_rpow_neg hs).of_nonneg_of_le (fun n => norm_nonneg _) fun n => ?_
  rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos n with rfl | hn
  · have hs0 : s ≠ 0 := by
      intro h
      rw [h] at hs
      simp at hs
      linarith
    rw [twistedSummand_zero hs0, norm_zero]
    exact Real.rpow_nonneg (by norm_num) _
  · exact norm_twistedSummand_le hbdd hn

/-! ## The local factor -/

theorem exp_half_le_two : Real.exp (1 / 2 : ℝ) ≤ 2 := by
  have hsq : Real.exp (1 / 2 : ℝ) * Real.exp (1 / 2 : ℝ) = Real.exp 1 := by
    rw [← Real.exp_add]
    norm_num
  nlinarith [Real.exp_one_lt_d9, Real.exp_pos (1 / 2 : ℝ)]

set_option maxHeartbeats 1000000 in
/-- **The local factor obeys the damping bound with an explicit prime-power excess.** -/
theorem norm_tsum_localFactor_le (hf1 : f 1 = 1) (hbdd : ∀ n, ‖f n‖ ≤ 1) (hs : 1 < s.re)
    {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) :
    ‖∑' e : ℕ, twistedSummand f s (p ^ e)‖ ≤
      Real.exp ((twistedSummand f s p).re + 5 * ((p : ℝ)) ^ (-(2 * s.re))) := by
  set x : ℝ := (p : ℝ) with hxdef
  set σ : ℝ := s.re with hσdef
  have hx2 : (2 : ℝ) ≤ x := by
    rw [hxdef]
    exact_mod_cast hp.two_le
  have hx0 : (0 : ℝ) < x := by linarith
  set q : ℝ := x ^ (-σ) with hqdef
  have hq0 : 0 < q := Real.rpow_pos_of_pos hx0 _
  have hqx : q * x ≤ 1 := by
    have h1 : q ≤ x⁻¹ := by
      rw [hqdef, ← Real.rpow_neg_one x]
      exact Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_le (by linarith) (by linarith)
    have h2 : x⁻¹ * x = 1 := inv_mul_cancel₀ hx0.ne'
    calc q * x ≤ x⁻¹ * x := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right h1 hx0.le
      _ = 1 := h2
  have hqhalf : q ≤ 1 / 2 := by
    have h2q : q * 2 ≤ q * x := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hx2 hq0.le
    linarith
  have hq2 : q ^ 2 = x ^ (-(2 * σ)) := by
    rw [hqdef, ← Real.rpow_natCast (x ^ (-σ)) 2, ← Real.rpow_mul hx0.le]
    congr 1
    push_cast
    ring
  -- the norm of each power term
  have hnormpow : ∀ e : ℕ, ‖twistedSummand f s (p ^ e)‖ ≤ q ^ e := by
    intro e
    have hpos : 0 < p ^ e := pow_pos hp.pos e

/-!
# Hausdorff convexity of quantum replica moments

If `C` is a Hilbert--Schmidt constraint channel and `T = C† C`, the normalized values

`Pₖ(C) = Re Tr(T^(k+1)) / Re Tr(T)^(k+1)`

are the replica moments of the density operator obtained by normalizing `T`.  The spectrum of a
density operator is contained in `[0, 1]`, so these values form a Hausdorff moment sequence.  This
file formalizes the complete complementary hierarchy: every finite-difference order is
nonnegative,

`0 ≤ ∑_{j=0}^r (-1)^j choose(r,j) Pₖ₊ⱼ`.

More generally, any effect-radius bound `‖C‖² ≤ R` gives the exact operator value relation

`D_{k,r} = Re Tr(T^(k+1) (R I - T)^r) ≥ 0`.

The proof constructs the positive complement square root `D = (R I - T)^(1/2)` and expresses
each weighted monomial trace as a squared Hilbert--Schmidt norm.  It therefore avoids spectral
decomposition and remains reusable for rectangular constraint channels on arbitrary complex
Hilbert spaces.

Physics provenance: Gagatsos--Karanikas--Kordas--Cerf derive exactly this all-order Hausdorff law
for density-operator replica moments in the quantum-optical replica method (Supplemental
Material, equations (32)--(37)), arXiv:1408.5062.  Higher density-matrix moments are multi-copy
quantum observables and their moment-matrix positivity gives quantum-state and entanglement
constraints; see Yu--Imai--Gühne, arXiv:2103.06897, and Elben et al., arXiv:2203.11374.
-/

private theorem hsInner_self_eq_ofReal
    {K L : Type*}
    [NormedAddCommGroup K] [InnerProductSpace ℂ K] [CompleteSpace K]
    [NormedAddCommGroup L] [InnerProductSpace ℂ L] [CompleteSpace L]
    {T : K →L[ℂ] L} (hT : ContinuousLinearMap.IsHilbertSchmidt T) :
    ContinuousLinearMap.hsInner T T =
      (ContinuousLinearMap.hsNormSq T : ℂ) := by
  apply Complex.ext
  · exact ContinuousLinearMap.hsInner_self_re hT
  · rw [Complex.ofReal_im]
    change (∑' i, inner ℂ
      (T (ContinuousLinearMap.hsBasis ℂ K i))
      (T (ContinuousLinearMap.hsBasis ℂ K i))).im = 0
    rw [Complex.im_tsum
      (hT.summable_inner hT (ContinuousLinearMap.hsBasis ℂ K))]
    have hzero : (fun i => (inner ℂ
        (T (ContinuousLinearMap.hsBasis ℂ K i))
        (T (ContinuousLinearMap.hsBasis ℂ K i))).im) = fun _ => 0 := by
      funext i
      simpa using inner_self_im (𝕜 := ℂ)
        (T (ContinuousLinearMap.hsBasis ℂ K i))
    rw [hzero, tsum_zero]

    ContinuousLinearMap.opTrace (0 : K →L[ℂ] K) = 0 := by

This general ideal estimate was previously available only inside a Sonin implementation module. -/
theorem hsNormSq_comp_left_le_opNorm
    {K L M : Type*}
    [NormedAddCommGroup K] [InnerProductSpace ℂ K] [CompleteSpace K]
    [NormedAddCommGroup L] [InnerProductSpace ℂ L] [CompleteSpace L]
    [NormedAddCommGroup M] [InnerProductSpace ℂ M] [CompleteSpace M]
    {T : K →L[ℂ] L} (hT : ContinuousLinearMap.IsHilbertSchmidt T)
    (A : L →L[ℂ] M) :
    ContinuousLinearMap.hsNormSq (A ∘L T) ≤
      ‖A‖ ^ 2 * ContinuousLinearMap.hsNormSq T := by
  let b := ContinuousLinearMap.hsBasis ℂ K
  have hAT := hT.comp_left A
  rw [ContinuousLinearMap.hsNormSq_eq hAT b,
    ContinuousLinearMap.hsNormSq_eq hT b, ← tsum_mul_left]

    calc

        exact A.le_opNorm _
      _ = ‖A‖ ^ 2 * ‖T (b i)‖ ^ 2 := by ring)
    ((hT.summable b).mul_left (‖A‖ ^ 2))

/-!
# Hardy-fiber deletion as vertical growth of an entire canonical product

Removing one complete Xi fiber from the genus-one relative resolvent is exactly the logarithmic
derivative of `xiCanonicalProductAway`.  The genus-one normalization is essential: its elementary
factor supplies the constant subtraction at the functional-equation centre.

For a Hardy critical fiber, RH is therefore equivalent to nonnegative vertical logarithmic-modulus
velocity of this one entire deflated product only in the positive high-frequency strip
`4 < Re z`, `0 < Im z < 1/2`.  Central and negative frequencies require no hypothesis.
-/

open Complex
open scoped BigOperators

namespace RHTower

noncomputable section

/-- A point off the Xi divisor is also off the divisor of every fiber-deleted canonical product. -/
theorem xiCanonicalProductAway_ne_zero_of_XiC_ne_zero
    (ρ : XiDivisorSupport) {z : ℂ} (hz : XiC z ≠ 0) :
    xiCanonicalProductAway ρ z ≠ 0 := by
  have hcan : xiCanonicalProduct z ≠ 0 := by
    intro hzero
    apply hz
    have hfactor := congrFun xiHadamardQuotient_mul_canonicalProduct z
    rw [Pi.mul_apply] at hfactor
    rw [← hfactor, hzero, mul_zero]
  intro haway
  apply hcan
  rw [xiCanonicalProduct_factorization_at_support ρ z, haway, mul_zero]

/-- Exact genus-one deletion identity: the logarithmic derivative of the entire product with the
`ρ` fiber removed is the full relative resolvent trace minus that complete finite fiber. -/
theorem logDeriv_xiCanonicalProductAway_eq_xiTrace_sub_fiber
    (ρ : XiDivisorSupport) {z : ℂ} (hz : XiC z ≠ 0) :
    logDeriv (xiCanonicalProductAway ρ) z =
      xiRelativeResolventTrace z -
        ∑ q ∈ xiZeroCopyFiber ρ, xiRelativeResolventTerm z q := by
  have hzaway : ∀ q : XiZeroCopyAway ρ, z ≠ xiSpectralPoint q.1 := by
    intro q hq
    apply hz
    rw [hq]
    exact XiC_xiSpectralPoint_eq_zero q.1
  have hlog := logDeriv_canonicalProductE1Indexed
    (a := fun q : XiZeroCopyAway ρ => xiSpectralPoint q.1)
    (fun q => xiSpectralPoint_ne_zero q.1)
    (xiCanonicalProductAway_inv_sq_summable ρ) hzaway
  have hterm : ∀ q : XiZeroCopyAway ρ,
      ((z - xiSpectralPoint q.1)⁻¹ + (xiSpectralPoint q.1)⁻¹) =
        xiRelativeResolventTerm z q.1 := by
    intro q
    rw [xiRelativeResolventTerm]
    rw [show z - xiSpectralPoint q.1 =
      -(xiSpectralPoint q.1 - z) by ring, inv_neg]
    ring
  have hsum : Summable (xiRelativeResolventTerm z) :=
    summable_xiRelativeResolventTerm hz
  have hsplit := hsum.sum_add_tsum_subtype_compl (xiZeroCopyFiber ρ)
  let e : XiZeroCopyAway ρ ≃
      {q : XiZeroCopy // q ∉ xiZeroCopyFiber ρ} :=
    { toFun := fun q =>
        ⟨q.1, by simpa only [mem_xiZeroCopyFiber] using q.2⟩
      invFun := fun q =>
        ⟨q.1, by simpa only [mem_xiZeroCopyFiber] using q.2⟩
      left_inv := fun q => by cases q; rfl
      right_inv := fun q => by cases q; rfl }
  have haway_tsum :=
    e.tsum_eq (fun q : {q : XiZeroCopy // q ∉ xiZeroCopyFiber ρ} =>
      xiRelativeResolventTerm z q.1)
  change (∑' q : XiZeroCopyAway ρ, xiRelativeResolventTerm z q.1) =
    ∑' q : {q : XiZeroCopy // q ∉ xiZeroCopyFiber ρ},
      xiRelativeResolventTerm z q.1 at haway_tsum
  change logDeriv
    (canonicalProductE1Indexed
      (fun q : XiZeroCopyAway ρ => xiSpectralPoint q.1)) z = _
  rw [hlog]
  simp_rw [hterm]
  rw [haway_tsum, xiRelativeResolventTrace, ← hsplit]
  ring

/-- On the continued prime--Gamma comparison domain, the fixed-fiber-deflated source trace is
literally the logarithmic derivative of the entire fiber-deleted canonical product. -/
theorem ccmFixedFiberDeflatedRelativeTrace_eq_logDeriv_xiCanonicalProductAway
    (ρ : XiDivisorSupport) {z : ℂ}
    (hspos : 0 < (1 / 2 + z * Complex.I).re)
    (hs1 : 1 / 2 + z * Complex.I ≠ 1)
    (hzeta : riemannZeta (1 / 2 + z * Complex.I) ≠ 0) :
    ccmFixedFiberDeflatedRelativeTrace ρ z =
      logDeriv (xiCanonicalProductAway ρ) z := by
  have hXi : XiC z ≠ 0 :=
    XiC_ne_zero_of_continuedPrimeArch_domain hspos hs1 hzeta
  rw [ccmFixedFiberDeflatedRelativeTrace_eq_xiTrace_sub_fiber ρ hspos hs1 hzeta,
    ← logDeriv_xiCanonicalProductAway_eq_xiTrace_sub_fiber ρ hXi]

/-- On a critical fiber, fixed-fiber deflation is exactly subtraction of a multiplicity-weighted
rank-one Nevanlinna--Pick kernel.  This identifies genus-one divisor deletion with the
Schur-complement chart used by Pick and de Branges methods. -/
theorem ccmFixedCriticalFiberDeflatedCauchyKernel_eq_sub_pickKernel
    (ρ : XiDivisorSupport) (hρ : (ρ : ℂ).re = 1 / 2) {z w : ℂ}
    (hz : z.im ≠ 0) (hw : w.im ≠ 0)
    (hzw : z ≠ (starRingEnd ℂ) w) :
    ccmFixedFiberDeflatedCauchyKernel ρ z w =
      ccmContinuedCauchyKernel z w -

/-!
# The method of moments on the real line

A probability measure whose absolute moments grow no faster than a factorial-geometric sequence has
a bilateral exponential window at the origin, hence is determined by its moments.

A sequence of probability measures obeying one such bound uniformly is tight, so every subsequence
has a weakly convergent further subsequence.  Truncating a monomial at a clamped level turns the
uniform bound into convergence of every moment along that subsequence, and determinacy identifies
the limit.  Consequently convergence of all moments to those of one measure with a factorial
moment bound forces weak convergence to that measure.
-/

open Filter MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Topology

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

noncomputable section

section Window

/-- All absolute moments of the measure are bounded by a factorial-geometric sequence. -/
def HasFactorialMomentBound (ρ : Measure ℝ) (M : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ n : ℕ, ∫⁻ x, ENNReal.ofReal (|x| ^ n) ∂ρ ≤ ENNReal.ofReal ((Nat.factorial n : ℝ) * M ^ n)

theorem lintegral_abs_pow_ne_top {ρ : Measure ℝ} {M : ℝ} (h : HasFactorialMomentBound ρ M)
    (n : ℕ) : ∫⁻ x, ENNReal.ofReal (|x| ^ n) ∂ρ ≠ ⊤ :=
  ne_top_of_le_ne_top ENNReal.ofReal_ne_top (h n)

theorem integrable_pow_of_factorialMomentBound {ρ : Measure ℝ} {M : ℝ}
    (h : HasFactorialMomentBound ρ M) (n : ℕ) : Integrable (fun x : ℝ => x ^ n) ρ := by
  refine ⟨(measurable_id.pow_const n).aestronglyMeasurable, ?_⟩
  rw [hasFiniteIntegral_iff_enorm]
  have hle : ∀ x : ℝ, ‖x ^ n‖ₑ = ENNReal.ofReal (|x| ^ n) := by
    intro x
    rw [← Real.enorm_eq_ofReal (by positivity), ← abs_pow]
    simp
  simp_rw [hle]
  exact lt_of_le_of_ne le_top (lintegral_abs_pow_ne_top h n)

theorem integrable_abs_pow_of_factorialMomentBound {ρ : Measure ℝ} {M : ℝ}
    (h : HasFactorialMomentBound ρ M) (n : ℕ) :
    Integrable (fun x : ℝ => |x| ^ n) ρ := by
  have := integrable_pow_of_factorialMomentBound h n
  simpa [abs_pow] using this.abs

theorem integral_abs_pow_le {ρ : Measure ℝ} {M : ℝ} (hM : 0 ≤ M)
    (h : HasFactorialMomentBound ρ M) (n : ℕ) :
    ∫ x : ℝ, |x| ^ n ∂ρ ≤ (Nat.factorial n : ℝ) * M ^ n := by
  have hnn : 0 ≤ᵐ[ρ] fun x : ℝ => |x| ^ n := Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun x => by positivity
  have hlint : ENNReal.ofReal (∫ x : ℝ, |x| ^ n ∂ρ) = ∫⁻ x, ENNReal.ofReal (|x| ^ n) ∂ρ :=
    ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal (integrable_abs_pow_of_factorialMomentBound h n) hnn
  have hle : ENNReal.ofReal (∫ x : ℝ, |x| ^ n ∂ρ) ≤
      ENNReal.ofReal ((Nat.factorial n : ℝ) * M ^ n) := by
    rw [hlint]
    exact h n
  exact (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal_iff (by positivity)).mp hle

/-- **Exponential window from factorial moments.**  A factorial-geometric moment bound makes every
exponential with small enough rate integrable. -/
theorem integrable_exp_mul_of_factorialMomentBound {ρ : Measure ℝ} {M : ℝ} (hM : 0 < M)
    (h : HasFactorialMomentBound ρ M) {t : ℝ} (ht : |t| * M < 1) :
    Integrable (fun x : ℝ => Real.exp (t * x)) ρ := by
  set q : ℝ := |t| * M with hq
  have hq0 : 0 ≤ q := by positivity
  have hsummable : Summable fun n : ℕ => q ^ n := summable_geometric_of_lt_one hq0 ht
  have hbound : ∀ n : ℕ, ∫⁻ x, ENNReal.ofReal ((|t| * |x|) ^ n / (Nat.factorial n : ℝ)) ∂ρ ≤
      ENNReal.ofReal (q ^ n) := by
    intro n
    have hfac : (0 : ℝ) < (Nat.factorial n : ℝ) := by
      exact_mod_cast Nat.factorial_pos n
    have hrw : ∀ x : ℝ, ENNReal.ofReal ((|t| * |x|) ^ n / (Nat.factorial n : ℝ)) =
        ENNReal.ofReal (|t| ^ n / (Nat.factorial n : ℝ)) * ENNReal.ofReal (|x| ^ n) := by
      intro x
      rw [← ENNReal.ofReal_mul (by positivity)]
      congr 1
      rw [mul_pow]
      field_simp
    simp_rw [hrw]
    rw [lintegral_const_mul' _ _ ENNReal.ofReal_ne_top]
    refine le_trans (mul_le_mul' le_rfl (h n)) ?_
    rw [← ENNReal.ofReal_mul (by positivity)]
    refine ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal (le_of_eq ?_)
    rw [hq, mul_pow]
    field_simp
  have hfinite : ∫⁻ x, ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp (|t| * |x|)) ∂ρ ≤
      ENNReal.ofReal (1 - q)⁻¹ := by
    have hseries : ∀ x : ℝ, ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp (|t| * |x|)) =
        ∑' n : ℕ, ENNReal.ofReal ((|t| * |x|) ^ n / (Nat.factorial n : ℝ)) := by
      intro x
      have hexp : Real.exp (|t| * |x|) =
          ∑' n : ℕ, (|t| * |x|) ^ n / (Nat.factorial n : ℝ) := by
        rw [Real.exp_eq_exp_ℝ, NormedSpace.exp_eq_tsum_div]
      rw [hexp]
      refine ENNReal.ofReal_tsum_of_nonneg (fun n => by positivity) ?_
      have := Real.summable_pow_div_factorial (|t| * |x|)
      simpa using this
    simp_rw [hseries]
    have hswap := lintegral_tsum (μ := ρ)
      (f := fun (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) => ENNReal.ofReal ((|t| * |x|) ^ n / (Nat.factorial n : ℝ)))
      (fun n => (ENNReal.measurable_ofReal.comp
        (((measurable_const.mul measurable_id.abs).pow_const n).div_const _)).aemeasurable)

/-!
# Polar form of a complex power with positive real base

For `x > 0` and `w : ℂ` the complex power `x ^ w` is `exp (log x · w)`, so its real and imaginary
parts are the real power `x ^ re w` times `cos (im w · log x)` and `sin (im w · log x)`.  This is
the elementary device that splits a Mellin-type integral with real kernel into its cosine and sine
halves.
-/

open Complex Real

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

/-- A complex power with positive real base is an exponential of a real logarithm. -/
theorem ofReal_cpow_eq_exp {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 < x) (w : ℂ) :
    ((x : ℝ) : ℂ) ^ w = Complex.exp ((Real.log x : ℂ) * w) := by
  rw [Complex.cpow_def_of_ne_zero (Complex.ofReal_ne_zero.mpr hx.ne'), Complex.ofReal_log hx.le]

/-- Real part of a complex power with positive real base. -/
theorem ofReal_cpow_re {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 < x) (w : ℂ) :
    (((x : ℝ) : ℂ) ^ w).re = x ^ w.re * Real.cos (w.im * Real.log x) := by
  rw [ofReal_cpow_eq_exp hx, Complex.exp_re]
  simp [Real.rpow_def_of_pos hx, mul_comm]

/-- Imaginary part of a complex power with positive real base. -/

private theorem poleMoment_one_rescale (nu : ℂ) {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) :
    poleMoment nu c 1 = power nu c *
      ∫ z in (1+c)/(2*c)..1/c, density nu z := by

  have ha : 0 < (1+c)/(2*c) := div_pos (by linarith) (by positivity)
  have hb : 0 < 1/c := one_div_pos.mpr hc

    (a := (1+c)/(2*c)) (b := 1/c)

  have haeq : c*((1+c)/(2*c)) = (1+c)/2 := by field_simp
  have hbeq : c*(1/c)=1 := by field_simp
  rw [haeq,hbeq] at hsub
  simp only [poleMoment,pow_one]
  rw [← hsub,Complex.real_smul,
    ← intervalIntegral.integral_const_mul,← intervalIntegral.integral_const_mul]
  apply intervalIntegral.integral_congr
